name: ARC (AI2 Reasoning Challenge)
description: The AI2 Reasoning Challenge (ARC) is a question set, text corpus, and baselines assembled to encourage AI research in advanced question answering. The ARC question set contains 7,787 natural, grade-school science questions (authored for human standardized tests), partitioned into a Challenge Set (2,590 questions answered incorrectly by both a retrieval-based algorithm and a word co-occurrence algorithm) and an Easy Set (5,197 questions). The dataset also includes the ARC Corpus, a corpus of 14M science sentences relevant to the task, and implementations of three neural baseline models (DecompAttn, BiDAF, and DGEM).
creator: Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence (AI2)
citeAs: Clark, P., Cowhey, I., Etzioni, O., Khot, T., Sabharwal, A., Schoenick, C., & Tafjord, O. (2018). Think you have Solved Question Answering? Try ARC, the AI2 Reasoning Challenge. arXiv:1803.05457v1 [cs.AI].
rai:dataCollection: The ARC dataset was assembled through several months of extensive search and investigation to collect natural science questions authored for use on standardized tests. Questions were drawn from a variety of public standardized test sources covering US elementary and middle school science. The ARC Corpus was created by utilizing a major search engine to run a large series of search queries relevant to science, with queries automatically constructed by instantiating 100 hand-written templates for 80 science topics covered by US elementary and middle schools.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Document analysis, Secondary Data analysis
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Questions were drawn from a variety of standardized test sources including ACTAAP, AIMS, Alaska Dept Ed, AMP, CA Standards Test, FCAT, LA Ed Assessment Program, MD School Assessment, MCAS, MEA, MEAP, Mercury (anonymous content partner of AI2), MSA, NAEP, NC READY, NY Regents, Ohio Achievement Tests, TAKS, TIMSS, VA Standards of Learning, and WASL. The ARC Corpus was built from web documents retrieved via a major search engine using science-related queries, augmented with the AristoMini corpus (dictionary definitions from Wiktionary, articles from Simple Wikipedia tagged as science, and additional science sentences from the Web).
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Questions were partitioned into a Challenge Set and an Easy Set based on whether both a retrieval-based (IR) algorithm and a word co-occurrence (PMI) algorithm answered them incorrectly. Questions answered incorrectly by both algorithms were placed in the Challenge Set (2,590 questions); the remainder formed the Easy Set (5,197 questions). The dataset includes the publicly releasable subset of the Kaggle Allen AI Science Challenge questions (about 60% of the Kaggle set, making up 43% of the ARC set).
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For the ARC Corpus, top documents retrieved from search queries were collected and de-duplicated, then content was stripped down to capture just the text in each document. The resulting text was chunked into sentences. The corpus was augmented with the AristoMini corpus. Only non-diagram, multiple-choice science questions were included in the dataset.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Elasticsearch (used for information retrieval in IR solver and entailment-based baselines); Open IE (used for structured representation extraction in DGEM and DGEM-OpenIE models); AllenNLP (framework for neural baseline models).
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The ARC Dataset, Corpus, three baseline neural models (DecompAttn, BiDAF, and DGEM), and a leaderboard are all publicly available at http://data.allenai.org/arc. An up-to-date leaderboard is maintained for tracking new results.
rai:dataSocialImpact: ARC is designed to encourage AI research in advanced question answering that requires reasoning, use of commonsense knowledge, and deeper text comprehension, moving beyond factoid-style QA. It aims to drive progress on more difficult AI challenges that standardized tests represent, which have been proposed as a Grand Challenge for AI.
rai:dataBiases: Large portions of standardized tests can be easily solved by simple AI methods (e.g., information retrieval, statistical correlations), causing scores to be dominated by simple algorithms and biasing research towards incrementally improving those algorithms. The Challenge Set partition was designed to mitigate this by excluding questions solvable by simple retrieval or co-occurrence methods. Approximately 75% of web documents collected for the ARC Corpus were judged as science relevant (from an informal analysis of a random sample of 805 documents).
rai:dataLimitations: The ARC Corpus, while covering knowledge relevant to approximately 95% of Challenge questions, cannot be fully exploited by simple retrieval methods. The Challenge Set definition only approximates the informal goal of 'hard' questions, as it is based on two specific baseline solvers. Questions are limited to non-diagram, multiple-choice science questions for US elementary and middle school grade levels (3rd to 9th grade). Only 11 question words (mainly proper nouns) do not appear in the ARC Corpus vocabulary.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for use in training, development, and testing of advanced question answering systems. It is partitioned into train, dev, and test sets for the Challenge and Easy sets. The ARC Corpus is provided as an optional resource for corpus-based approaches. Systems are not restricted to the provided corpus. The leaderboard supports ongoing benchmarking of new QA models.
